div.head: Rect 6.2, 6.3, 6.4
div.ab: [6.2] gyme eac swan, þæt he æfter sticunge his slyhtswyn wel behweorfe [7] sæncge; ðonne bið he ful wel gewyrces wyrðe. [6.3] Eac he sceal beon – swa ic ær be beocere cwæð – oftræde to gehwilcon weorce 7 gehorsad to hlafordes neode. [6.4] Ðeow swan 7 ðeow beocere æfter forðsiðe be anre lage wyrðe.

[6.2] Uiderit etiam porcarius, ut post occisam ipsam porcos occisos bene correddiet et suspendat: et tunc habeatur dignus opera sua. [6.3] Etiam erit, sicut de custode apum diximus, multis operibus frequentatus et equum habeat in opus domini sui. [6.4] Seruus porcarius et seruus custos apum post obitum suum sint unius legis digni.

On manegum lan|dum gebyreð deopre swanriht. gyme eac swan þæt he æfter sticunge his slyhtswyn wel behweor|fe sæncge . ðonne bið he ful wel gewyrces wyr|ðe . eac he sceal beon swa ic ær be beocere cwæð. oftræde to gehwilcon weorce. 7 gehorsad to hlafordes neode . ðeowswan . 7 ðeow beoce|re . æfter forðsiðe be anre lage wyrðe .

Gyme eac swan, þæt he æfter sticunge his slyhtswyn wel behweorfe and sæncge: ðonne bið he ful wel gewyrces wyrðe. [6.3] Eac he sceal beon swa ic ær be beocere cwæð, oftræde to gehwilcon weorce and gehorsad to hlafordes neode. [6.4] Ðeow swan and ðeow beocere æfter forðsiðe be anre lage wyrðe.

On many estates deeper duties are owed from the swineherd. Also, the duty of the swineherd is that he sends slaughtered pigs well-prepared after [their] slaughter, then he will be full-well worth his perquisites. Also, just as I said before concerning the beekeeper, he must be ready all the while to work, and horsed for the lord’s needs. The bound swineherd and the bound beekeeper, after departing, are worthy of the same law.

Furthermore, the swineherd should take care that each swine after it is slaughtered be well prepared and smoked; then will he be fully worthy of his privileges. [6.3] Also, as I said before concerning the beekeeper, he must always be ready to take on any task, and equipped with a horse for his lord’s needs. [6.4] After their death, the peasant swineherd and the peasant beekeeper are subject to the same law.

[6.2] Achte auch der Schweinehirt, dass er nach der Abstechung seine Schlachtschweine gut herrichte [ausbreite] und [Borsten] absenge: dann ist er recht wohl [zum Empfange] des Eingeweides berechtigt. [6.3] Auch muss er — wie ich vorhin vom Bienenmann gesagt habe — oft zu jeder Frohnarbeit bereit und für des Herrn Bedarf mit einem Pferde versehen sein. [6.4] Unfreier Schweinehirt und unfreier Bienenmann sei nach dem Tode derselben Rechtsregel [nämlich dass der Herr den Nachlass nimmt; wie 5.5] unterworfen.

[6.2] Let the swineherd also take care that after the slaughter he prepare [lay out] his slaughter-pigs well and singe [the bristles]: then he is well entitled [to receive] the entrails. [6.3] He must also — as I said before of the bee-keeper — be ready often for every labour-service, and be provided with a horse for the lord's needs. [6.4] An unfree swineherd and an unfree bee-keeper shall after death be subject to the same rule of law [namely that the lord takes what they leave; as 5.5].
div.note: This row combines Liebermann's 6.2–6.4. ‘[⁊]’ is lacking in B and supplied from the Quadripartitus. The Quadripartitus translates Middle English ‘henge’ (hang) for ‘sæncge’ and ‘geweorces’ for ‘gewyrces’. ‘Ðeow’ as an adjective, with Toller; earlier (also Toller) ‘þeowswan ⁊ þeowbeocere’. B's ‘be’ stands so. Liebermann compares 5.2 f., 7 and 18.
This row holds several of Rabin’s sections (6.2, 6.3, 6.4), each marked with its number.
